subject: MSA / Order Form: SLA maintenance window & credit boundaries
messages:
From: Amy Liu <amy.liu@orioninc.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@orioninc.com
Date: 2026-12-12T18:05:00Z
Subject: Orion Order Form / SLA redlines attached

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our legal team attached a first-pass set of redlines to the Order Form and SLA — please see attached (Orion_SLA_Redline_v1.pdf). The main open items:

- Availability target: we redlined to 99.9% and requested a 30% monthly service credit for downtime below the target.
- Maintenance windows: we requested the ability to schedule weekly maintenance windows not to exceed 6 hours per week, with 72-hour advance notice.
- Response times: P1 1 hour, P2 4 hours, P3 24 hours (we included stricter definitions).
- Credit cap: we proposed there be no annual cap given the potential business impact.

Can your team confirm whether Redwood can accept these items as-is, or if you need counterproposals? We have an internal procurement timeline — hoping to finalize by next Wednesday (2026-12-16).

Attached: Orion_SLA_Redline_v1.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Amy Liu
Head of Procurement, Orion Inc.
amy.liu@orioninc.com

--
On 2026-12-11 Amy and Vanessa had a 20-minute kickoff call to confirm scope and pilot schedule. This email summarizes next steps from legal.

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amy Liu <amy.liu@orioninc.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T14:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Orion Order Form / SLA redlines attached

Amy — thanks for sending these over and for the timeline. I pulled in Neha (sales ops) and Markus (legal liaison) to run through the specifics. Quick summary of Redwood's initial position:

- Availability target: Redwood's standard enterprise SLO is 99.95% for dedicated deployments. We can consider 99.9% for an initial pilot but would need a defined rollback/upgrade path to 99.95% for production.
- Service credits: a 30% monthly credit is unusually high relative to industry norms; Redwood typically proposes a declining credit curve tied to severity and incident count with a combined monthly cap. Proposed counter: up to 15% monthly credit with an annual cap of 3 months' equivalent fees.
- Maintenance windows: 6 hours/week is ok for scheduled, non-overlapping maintenance; we request grouping routine maintenance into a single weekly window not exceeding 8 hours, and a maximum of 72 hours advance notice only for scheduled platform upgrades (not emergency patches).
- Response times: our definitions align on P1/P2/P3 but we typically define P1 as residual production-down incidents with a 30-minute acknowledge and 2-hour target resolution SLA for critical infra — we can accept 1-hour acknowledge and 4-hour response for application-level P1 if Orion will commit to the escalation matrix.

I'm attaching the internal comment set (Redwood_SLA_Comments_v1.docx) and a tracker that highlights where we need legal signoff. Can you confirm which items are deal-breakers for Orion vs negotiable? If you can loop procurement/legal in with a prioritized list, we'll aim for a redline back by EOD Tuesday (2026-12-15).

Next steps I propose:
- You flag the three non-negotiables from Orion (availability, credit cap, and maintenance notice).
- We will prepare a compromise redline and call it out in the tracker.
- If Orion needs the 30% credit, we'll need approval from Sales Leadership (Karthik copied) due to margin impact.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Comments_v1.docx (DOCX)

Thanks — Van
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0119

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-13T16:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Orion Order Form / SLA redlines attached (internal notes)

Vanessa / Markus / Karthik — internal notes following Amy's redline:

- Financial exposure: if we accept 30% monthly credit with no cap, modeled annual exposure exceeds 20% of committed ARR for a 3-month outage scenario. Sales leadership will not approve without mitigation (either cap or credit tapering).
- Suggested compromise language: 15% credit for the first qualifying month, 10% for second, then escalate to 5% thereafter, with an annual cap equal to 3 months' fees or a fixed dollar cap (whichever is lower).
- Maintenance definition: recommend we define "Scheduled Maintenance" vs "Emergency Maintenance". Scheduled requires 72-hour notice and cannot exceed 8 hours/week. Emergency maintenance (security fixes) allowed with best-effort notice; exclude emergency maintenance from credit calculations if we can show reasonable mitigation.
- P1 handling: require an agreed-upon runbook and weekly / on-demand war room as acceptance criteria for P1 resolution commitments.

Action items for us:
1) Vanessa to present the adjusted credit curve and maintenance grouping to Amy.
2) Markus to prepare two alternative legal clauses (credit cap vs fixed dollar cap) for negotiation.
3) Karthik to confirm whether Sales Leadership will entertain a temporary 99.9% pilot commitment.

Attaching: Redline_Tracker.xlsx (XLSX)

Neha
Senior Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amy Liu <amy.liu@orioninc.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, contracts@orioninc.com
Date: 2026-12-14T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Orion Order Form / SLA redlines attached — consolidated counterproposal and next steps

Amy — appreciate the quick turnaround. After internal review we've put together a consolidated counterproposal so Orion's procurement/legal can see a single set of tradeoffs. Key points: 

1) Availability target
- Pilot: Accept 99.9% for an initial 90-day pilot on dedicated capacity.
- Production: Commitment to move to 99.95% within 60 days of pilot completion contingent on observed load and KV cache sizing.

2) Service credits and cap
- Proposed credit curve: 15% for first qualifying month, 10% for second, 5% thereafter for consecutive months.
- Annual cap: three months' equivalent fees OR a fixed-dollar cap of $250,000 (whichever is lower).
- Credits are cumulative by incident but subject to the annual cap.

3) Maintenance windows
- Scheduled Maintenance: grouped into a single weekly window (up to 8 hours) with 72-hour notice.
- Emergency Maintenance: excluded from credit calculations if Redwood provides evidence of critical risk remediation; Redwood will notify asap and provide timeline updates.

4) Response / escalation
- Acknowledge P1 within 30 minutes; target mitigations within 2 hours for infra-level incidents. We will provide a runbook and a shared war-room for the pilot period.

5) Implementation items
- Markus will send two legal clause options (credit cap vs fixed dollar cap) by EOD today for you to review.
- We can accept limited exceptions only with Sales Leadership approval; Karthik (cc) will confirm by EOD if we can make a one-time exception for a higher credit cap.

Requested next steps from Orion:
- Please confirm which items are absolute requirements vs negotiable (availability target, credit cap, maintenance notice).
- If acceptable, we will prepare an updated Order Form and circulate for execution. I added a HubSpot link and a draft DocuSign envelope here so procurement can see the timeline: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/5721 and https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning?envelopeId=0a1b2c

Attachments: Redline_Tracker.xlsx (XLSX), OrderForm_Draft.docx (DOCX)

If you'd prefer a 30-minute call to finalize language, I'm available today 15:00-17:00 PT.

Thanks — look forward to your note.
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
